quandoUsar: Async actions that should show progress and confirmation on the button itself: save draft, publish, sync.
When you want the pending and done states managed by the component from a single `onAction` function.
quandoEvitar: Use `button` when you need variants, sizes, or your own icon: here the look is fixed, filled, with an arrow on the right.
Use `action-swap` when the button toggles between states that persist, like Follow and Following, or needs a tone and icon per state.
Use `confirm-morph` or `hold-to-confirm` when the action is destructive and needs confirmation before it runs.

teclado.acao: Trigger `onAction`; while the action is pending, further activations are ignored.

acessibilidade: It is a native `<button>` with `type="button"` by default; while pending, it gets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`, so focus is not lost mid-action.
The animated text and the icons are `aria-hidden`: the screen reader gets the fixed `label` and a `role="status"` that announces `pendingLabel` and then `successLabel`.
`pendingLabel` and `successLabel` default to English (“Saving” and “Saved”); pass both in the interface language.
movimento: The label swaps with a short fade (the new one rises 2 px) and the button width follows the text with a spring with no overshoot.
The arrow exits to the right when the action starts, gives way to a spinner and then to a checkmark that draws itself; on return to rest, the arrow enters from the left.
With “reduce motion”, the label swaps instantly, the icons only fade, the width jumps, the checkmark appears already drawn, and the spinner does not spin.
responsivo: The label does not wrap and the width changes with each state; in tight rows, use text of similar length in `label`, `pendingLabel`, and `successLabel` so neighbors do not shift.
desempenho: Each button keeps a `ResizeObserver` to measure the label and a timer to return to rest; avoid hundreds of them in a long list.
notasIA: The action goes in `onAction` (there is no `onClick`): return a Promise so the pending state lasts while it runs, and reject it to signal failure.
On failure the button returns to rest with no message and calls `onActionError`; show the error yourself, for example with `toast`.
`resetAfterMs` (default 2400) sets how long the done state stays visible; with `0` it stays until the next click.

quandoUsar: An action that cycles through a few related states in the same place, like Follow, Following, and Unfollow.
Short submissions with a transient confirmation: “Send invoice” becomes “Sending”, then “Sent”, and returns to the start on its own with `holdFor`.
When each state needs its own icon and tone (`neutral`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, or `quiet`).
quandoEvitar: Use `action-button` when there is a single action with pending and done states and you do not want to describe states.
Use `split-button` when the person chooses among alternatives: here each click only advances to the next state in the list.
Use `switch` when the control represents an on or off setting, not an action.

teclado.acao: Advance to the next state in `states` (after the last, back to the first), calling `onAction` first.

acessibilidade: It is a `<button>` whose `aria-label` follows the visible label; while `onAction` runs, it gets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` and stays focusable.
Each change is announced by a `role="status"` next to the button: the new `label`, the `pendingLabel`, or the `failureLabel`.
Without a `pendingLabel` on the target state, the wait announcement is the fixed text “Working”; set `pendingLabel` and `failureLabel` (default “Try again”) in the interface language.
movimento: Letters shared at the start and end of the label stay still and the new ones rise from a slight blur, in sequence, while the width follows a spring with no overshoot.
Without `pendingLabel`, the pill folds into a circle with a spinner while the Promise runs (at least 450 ms); a failure shows `failureLabel` for 1.8 s and returns to the current state.
With “reduce motion”, letters and icons swap with a 0.12 s fade, the width jumps, and the spinner does not spin.
responsivo: Labels do not wrap and the pill changes width with each state; keep each `label` short.
desempenho: Each letter of the label is an animated element and there is one `ResizeObserver` per button: it suits short labels, not sentences.
notasIA: Describe the states in `states` (`id`, `label`, `icon`, `tone`) in cycle order; with fewer than two states the button is disabled.
`onAction(next, current)` runs before the swap: return a Promise to show the wait phase and reject it to display `failureLabel`.
Control the state with `value` and `onValueChange` or leave it internal with `defaultValue`; `holdFor` on a state makes the button advance on its own after that time.

quandoUsar: Any single action on a page, form, or dialog: save, continue, cancel.
Actions whose label changes in place, like “Save” becoming “Saved”: the width follows the new text with a spring, with no jump.
Short async work where a loading indicator on the button itself is enough feedback (`loading` prop).
quandoEvitar: Use `action-button` when the button needs to show the pending and done states by itself after an async action.
Use `split-button` when the main action has close alternatives in a menu.
Use `hold-to-confirm` for destructive actions that need more than a click.

teclado.acao: Trigger the button; with `loading`, the activation is ignored.
Moves focus to the next control; the focus ring only appears with the keyboard (`:focus-visible`, a `foundation.css` rule).

acessibilidade: It is a native `<button>`: role, focus, and keyboard activation come from the browser.
During `loading` the button gets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, stays focusable, and keeps the label in the DOM for screen readers.
On an icon-only button, pass `aria-label` with the action name.
movimento: The press slightly reduces the button scale; anchors of menus and popovers do not scale, so the panel measures the right size.
When the content changes, the width animates with a spring with no overshoot and the label swaps with a short fade.
With “reduce motion”, the press scale and the width spring are turned off, the label swaps with a 0.12 s fade, and the loading indicator does not spin.
responsivo: The label does not wrap (`white-space: nowrap`); on narrow screens prefer short labels or the `sm` size.
Minimum heights come from the `--control-height-sm`, `-md`, and `-lg` tokens, so they follow the rest of the controls.
desempenho: Measuring the label width uses one observer per button; it is cheap, but avoid hundreds of them in a long list.
notasIA: Default choice for a single action; for a row of actions with icons prefer `floating-button-group` or `button-group`, and with close alternatives, `split-button`.
Pass the changing label (Save → Saved) as the child to get the width animation with no configuration; `loading` blocks `onClick` without disabling the button.

Variants `primary` (default), `secondary`, `ghost`, and `danger`, sizes `sm`, `md`, and `lg`; the component does not set `type`, so inside a `<form>` pass `type="button"` when the action does not submit.

quandoUsar: Related actions on the same object that should read as a single control: Share, Download, Archive.
When the less-used actions fit in a menu attached to the end of the row (`menu` prop).
Bars where labels can shrink to icons when width runs short (`collapseLabels`).
quandoEvitar: Use `toggle-group` or `segmented-control` when the buttons represent a state or a choice: here no segment is marked as pressed.
Use `split-button` when there is a main action and the others are alternatives to it.
Use `overflow-actions` when the bar should send the actions that do not fit the width to a menu.

teclado.acao: Move through each segment in order; all of them are tab stops.
Move focus between segments and wrap around at the ends; in the `vertical` orientation `↓` and `↑` apply, and in RTL the arrows are reversed.
Move focus to the first and last segment.
Trigger the focused segment (a segment with `href` is a link and responds only to `Enter`); on the arrow, open the menu.
On the arrow, opens the menu; inside it, `↓` and `↑` loop through the items and `Enter` selects.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the arrow.

acessibilidade: The container is `role="group"` with the required `label` as its name; each segment is a `<button>` or, with `href`, a link.
`iconOnly` segments, with `content`, or collapsed ones use the `label` as `aria-label` (and, with no visible text, also as `title`); a `disabled` item becomes `aria-disabled` and stays focusable.
A label that changes right after the segment itself is triggered, like “Copied”, is announced once by an `aria-live="polite"` region.
movimento: A single highlight slides between segments under the pointer or keyboard focus, on a spring with no overshoot, and neighboring dividers disappear so it reads as one shape.
The press shrinks only the segment content (0.97; 0.9 on icon ones); a new label rises from a slight blur inside a fixed-width box when `reserve` lists the texts.
With “reduce motion”, the highlight jumps to the segment, there is no press scale, and the menu only fades.
responsivo: With `collapseLabels` (default), when the row does not fit the container, segments with an icon hide the label, which moves to `aria-label` and `title`, and get it back when there is room again.
The group never exceeds 100% of the container: what is left over scrolls horizontally with no visible scrollbar; in the `vertical` orientation the segments take the full width and do not collapse.
desempenho: Each group uses `ResizeObserver` on the parent container, on itself, and on each segment, and tests segment positions on every pointer move: suited to bars, not to dozens of groups in a list.
notasIA: `label` names the group and is required; each item needs `id` and `label`, and the action goes in `onSelect` (or `href`, for the segment to become a link).
If a label changes (Share → Copied), list all the texts in `reserve` so the segment keeps the width of the longest.
It is a group of actions with no selected state; `menu` (`label` and `items`) adds the arrow with the menu, and `variant="solid"` is the filled, more prominent version.

quandoUsar: Destructive actions where a modal dialog would be heavy: delete a project, revoke access, discard a draft.
When the question, the progress, and the result with Undo should happen in place of the button itself.
Actions that need an extra barrier: `confirmMode="hold"` requires holding down and `countdown` gives a few seconds to cancel.
quandoEvitar: Use `dialog` when the person needs to read consequences or fill something in before confirming: here the question is a short line.
Use `hold-to-confirm` when holding the button is enough, with no question or Cancel.
Use `toast-action` when the action can run right away and Undo comes afterward, in a notice.

teclado.acao: On the resting button, open the question and move focus to the confirm button, where the same keys confirm (in `countdown` mode, they start the countdown).
Toggle between Cancel and Confirm.
Cancels the question or the countdown; on a result or error, returns to rest.
During the countdown, with focus on the control, runs the action without waiting for the end.
In `hold` mode, must stay pressed on the confirm button until the fill completes; releasing early undoes it.

acessibilidade: Focus follows the faces if it was already on the control: it goes to Confirm on the question, to the root during the countdown and the wait, to Undo or Try again on the result, and back to the button at rest.

The question is a `role="group"` labeled by the `prompt`, the root gets `aria-busy` while waiting, and a `role="status"` announces progress, result, and error, and also the question when `prompt` is text.

The timeout only pauses with the pointer over the control or with the tab hidden, not with keyboard focus; increase or zero out `confirmTimeout` and `resultTimeout` for keyboard or screen reader users.
movimento: A single pill changes width with a spring with no overshoot on each face; faces swap by fading, at natural width, and the parts of the new one enter in sequence from a slight blur.
In `hold` mode the confirm button fills from the left while pressed and empties on a spring if released early; in `countdown` a ring runs out and the seconds swap in place; success draws a checkmark.
With “reduce motion”, the width jumps, the faces only fade, the checkmark appears already drawn, and the wait indicator spins more slowly (1.6 s per turn).
responsivo: Nothing wraps: the question takes up to `16rem` (the excess becomes an ellipsis) and is followed by Cancel and Confirm, in a single row.
The pill does not exceed 100% of the container and clips what is left over; since Confirm comes last, in a narrow space it ends up outside the visible area: reserve width or shorten `prompt`.
notasIA: `onConfirm` can return a Promise: while it runs the wait face appears, a rejection shows the error with Try again, and passing `onUndo` adds Undo to the result.

Labels default to English and to deletion (`confirmLabel` “Delete”, `pendingLabel` “Deleting”, `doneLabel` “Deleted”): pass `prompt` and all the labels; announcements like “Cancelled” and “Undone” are fixed in the code.
It works with no external control; use `state` with `onStateChange` only if the parent needs to drive the faces, and `tone="neutral"` for important but reversible actions.

quandoUsar: Secondary actions on an object the person is already looking at, like a file, a card, or a project, opened with a right-click on the object itself.
Surfaces that should not show a menu button, but whose actions must remain reachable by keyboard (`Shift + F10` or the menu key).
quandoEvitar: Use `dropdown-menu` when the actions need a visible trigger or separators between groups; this menu is a flat list opened over the object.
Avoid on objects that already respond to clicks, like links, cards that open, or selectable rows: a simple click or tap anywhere on the target also opens the menu.
Use `swipe-actions` when each list row's actions should appear with a swipe gesture on touch.

teclado.acao: With focus on the target, open the menu just below it, with focus on the first enabled item.
Move through the enabled items and wrap around at the ends.
Go to the first and last enabled item.
Select the focused item, close the menu, and return focus to the target.
With focus in the menu, closes it and returns focus to the target.

acessibilidade: The target is a `<div>` with `tabIndex=0`, `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-label`; the menu is `role="menu"`, with `role="menuitem"` items, and gets the same `label` (default in English, “Context menu”).

On open, focus goes to the first enabled item, but the menu does not trap focus: `Tab` leaves it without closing it and, with focus outside, `Esc` no longer closes it (only a tap outside or scrolling).
`checked` does not become `aria-checked` and only draws a checkmark when the item has no `icon`; the state does not reach the screen reader.
movimento: The menu grows from the click point (the origin stays at the pointer even when the menu is pushed into the screen) on a short spring, and leaves fading faster than it entered.
Items enter in sequence, 35 ms apart, and a single highlight slides between rows under the pointer; with the keyboard, it jumps straight to the focused item.
With “reduce motion”, the menu only fades, items appear with no sequence, and the highlight does not slide.
responsivo: The menu uses `position: fixed` and is pushed to stay 8 px from the window edges; above 300 px in height (or the screen height) it scrolls inside, and long labels end in an ellipsis.
It closes when the page scrolls or the window is resized, instead of following the target.
notasIA: Wrap the object: `<ContextMenu label="Ações do arquivo" items={itens}>…</ContextMenu>`; the target becomes a block `<div>`, and each item needs `id` and `label`, with the action in `onSelect`.
Give every item an `icon`: without one an ellipsis icon appears, and `checked` only swaps that icon for a checkmark; `destructive` paints the item with the danger color.
Do not put links or buttons inside the target expecting them to work on their own: the click on them bubbles up to the target and also opens the menu.

quandoUsar: Next to a value the person will paste elsewhere: an install command, an API key, an invite link.
In tables, cards, and read-only fields, icon-only (`iconOnly`) or borderless (`variant="plain"`) to take little space.
quandoEvitar: Use `code-block` to display code snippets: it already includes this button.
When copying is a menu item or part of another control, use the `useCopyFeedback` hook (installed alongside, in `lib/use-copy-feedback.ts`) instead of nesting this button.

teclado.acao: Copy `value` and show the confirmation on the button itself.

acessibilidade: It is a `<button type="button">` whose accessible name is always `label`; the visible word and the icons are `aria-hidden`.
The result is announced in an `aria-live="polite"` region as “`label`: Copied” or “`label`: Could not copy”; the button name does not change.
In the `iconOnly` version, `label` is the button's only name: pass text that says what is copied, like “Copy link”.
movimento: On copy, the icon swaps for a checkmark that draws itself (or for an alert, on failure) and the word swaps with a short fade; the width follows the new word on a spring with no overshoot.
The press reduces the scale to 0.97 (0.96 for icon-only) and releases on a spring curve; after 1.9 s the button returns to the original label.
With “reduce motion”, swaps are instant, the checkmark appears already drawn, the width jumps, and the press does not change the scale.
notasIA: Pass the exact text in `value` and a short `label`; `onCopied` only runs when the copy succeeds, and failure shows on the button itself for 1.9 s.
“Copied”, “Failed”, and the announcements are fixed in English; in a Portuguese interface, replace those strings in the installed file.
Copying uses the Clipboard API and, if it is missing or refused (iframes, insecure context), falls back to a hidden `<textarea>` with `execCommand("copy")`.

quandoUsar: The main call to action of a marketing page or the end of a section, with `ArrowButton` (“Start free trial”) or `MagneticButton` (“Schedule a demo”).
Confirming something that should not happen from an accidental tap, like a payment, with `SlideToConfirm`.
quandoEvitar: Use `button` for common interface actions, like forms, dialogs, and toolbars; these three are showcase buttons.
Use `hold-to-confirm` or `confirm-morph` when the confirmation needs to fit in a button-sized control: `SlideToConfirm` is a 52 px tall track that takes the parent's width.

teclado.acao: On `ArrowButton` and `MagneticButton`, trigger the button; with `href` they are links and respond only to `Enter`.
On `SlideToConfirm`, with focus on the thumb, confirm directly, without dragging.

acessibilidade: `ArrowButton` and `MagneticButton` are native `<button>`, or `<a>` when they get `href`; on `ArrowButton`, the colored copy of the label is `aria-hidden`, and the name is the children's text.

On `SlideToConfirm`, the thumb is a button with an `aria-label` equal to `label` (afterward, `confirmedLabel`); keyboard activation confirms without dragging, and a `role="status"` announces the confirmation.
The track text is `aria-hidden` and the defaults are in English (“Slide to confirm”, “Confirmed”): write the whole action in `label`, like “Slide to pay R$ 48”.
movimento: `ArrowButton`: on hover, keyboard focus, or press, the arrow disc grows to cover the button (0.48 s), the label changes color at the fill edge, and a new arrow enters from the left.
`MagneticButton`: with the mouse within `reach` px, the button follows the cursor on a loose spring, with a slight sway on return, and the label moves a bit further; touch and pen move nothing.

`SlideToConfirm`: the thumb arrows nudge every 1.8 s and releasing before `threshold` (90%) returns it on a spring; with “reduce motion”, none of this animates, the magnet stops, and `ArrowButton` fills with no transition.
responsivo: `SlideToConfirm` takes the parent's width up to `20rem` and measures the track with an observer, so the thumb travel adjusts; with `touch-action: pan-y`, vertical scrolling still works over it.
On `ArrowButton`, the label does not wrap and ends in an ellipsis when space runs out.
desempenho: Each `MagneticButton` listens to `pointermove` on the whole window and measures its own position on every mouse move; use few per page.
notasIA: They are three exports from the same file: `import ArrowButton, { MagneticButton, SlideToConfirm } from "@/components/ryan-ui/cta-buttons/cta-buttons"` (the default is `ArrowButton`).

On `SlideToConfirm`, the action goes in `onConfirm`, which runs once (a simple tap only wiggles the thumb); to control it, use `confirmed` with `onConfirmedChange`, and `resetAfter` to return to the start on its own.

`ArrowButton` and `MagneticButton` become links with `href`; `ArrowButton` accepts `icon` in place of the arrow and `size` `md` or `lg`, and `MagneticButton` accepts `strength` (0 turns off the magnet) and `reach`.

quandoUsar: An app or area launcher at the bottom of a screen, with few icons and one active item.
Demo or creative interfaces where magnification under the cursor is part of the identity.
quandoEvitar: Use `floating-button-group` for work toolbars, with labels and shortcuts, where tiles that grow and bounce would get in the way.
Use `bounce-sidebar` or `animated-sidebar` for the main navigation of an app with many sections and always-visible names.
Avoid as the only navigation on narrow screens: on touch there is no magnification or name bubble, and the row does not adapt to the width.

teclado.acao: Move focus between enabled tiles and wrap around at the ends; the focused tile is magnified as if the cursor were over it.
Go to the first and last enabled tile.
Trigger the tile: it bounces, becomes the active one, and calls `onValueChange` and `onSelect`.

acessibilidade: The container is `role="toolbar"` with `aria-label` (default in English, “Dock”); each tile is a `<button>` with an `aria-label` equal to `label` and `aria-pressed` marking the active one.
The name bubble is visual only (`aria-hidden`) and appears with the pointer or keyboard focus; the `open` dot is also decorative and is not announced.
All tiles are `Tab` stops, in addition to the arrows; `separatorBefore` inserts a vertical `role="separator"`.
movimento: With mouse or pen, each tile grows with the cursor's proximity, on a curve that fades out at `range` px (140), smoothed by a spring; the tile under the cursor reaches `magnification` times its size (1.6).
On press, the tile makes two hops, one high and one low (0.62 s); the dot under the active one stretches into a short bar, and the name bubble rises and fades above the tile.
On touch there is no magnification or bubble; with “reduce motion”, there is also no magnification or hops, and the bubble only fades.
responsivo: The dock does not scroll or wrap: tiles have a fixed width (`size`), and in a container narrower than the row they overflow; size `size` and the number of items for the smallest screen.
Tiles grow upward from the bar's base, which keeps its height; leave free space above the dock for the magnified tiles and the bubble.
desempenho: On every pointer move over the dock, each tile measures its own position and animates its size on a spring; think a dozen tiles, not dozens.
notasIA: Each item needs `id`, `label`, and `icon` (an SVG of about 45% of `size`); control the active one with `value` and `onValueChange`, or leave it internal with `defaultValue`.
`open` draws the “running” dot, `separatorBefore` a divider before the item, and `disabled` leaves it visible but inert; `size`, `magnification`, and `range` tune the magnification.
Give the parent space above the dock (the demo uses `padding-top` of `--space-12`) and width for the whole row.

quandoUsar: A short set of actions on the page or an object, behind a labeled button, like “Project actions”.
Choices like “Sort by”, where the trigger itself shows the current option: change `label` and the new text enters animated, with the trigger width following on a spring.
quandoEvitar: Use `select` when the choice is a form value with the option marked: here the items are actions, with no selected state.
Use `split-button` when a main action should run on a click and the others are alternatives to it.
Use `context-menu` for actions opened with a right-click on the object itself, with no visible trigger.

teclado.acao: On the trigger, open the menu with focus on the first item.
Move through the enabled items and wrap around at the ends.
Go to the first and last item; `Page Up` and `Page Down` do the same.
Typing the start of a label moves focus to that item.
Select the focused item and close the menu.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.

acessibilidade: Uses Radix's `DropdownMenu`: the trigger gets `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls`, items are `role="menuitem"`, and `disabled` items are dimmed and skipped by the arrows.
The menu is modal: while open, focus is trapped in it, the page does not scroll, the rest is hidden from screen readers, and a click outside only closes the menu.
The trigger always shows the `label` text, which also names the menu; the icons on the trigger and items are decorative.
movimento: The menu appears offset 5 px toward the trigger and at 0.97 scale, via a CSS transition, and leaves faster than it entered; items enter in sequence, 35 ms apart.
A single highlight slides between items on a spring under the pointer and jumps straight with the arrows; the trigger arrow rotates 180° with the menu open.
With “reduce motion”, the menu only fades, items appear together, and the highlight, the arrow, and the trigger label swap with no animation.
responsivo: The menu is aligned to the end of the trigger, stays 12 px from the window edges, flips sides if there is not enough room, and never exceeds the available width; the trigger label ends in an ellipsis when space runs out.
notasIA: Pass `label` and `items` (each with `label`, `onSelect`, and, if you want, `icon`, `disabled`, `destructive`, and `separatorBefore`); the item's `label` is also the React key, so do not repeat labels.
The trigger is fixed (`label` text, optional `icon`, and an arrow) and the open state is internal: there is no prop for another trigger, for an icon-only button, or to control `open`.
Items show no selection mark; for a value selector, prefer `select`, or show the current choice in the `label` itself.

quandoUsar: A row of icons where only the control in use shows its name, like Share, Save, and Notify on an article.
Filters or states in chip form (`variant="chip"`) that, when active, show the value and a clear action, like “Status: Open ×”.
quandoEvitar: Use `expanding-button-group` when the icons form a single bar and the label should follow the pointer or focus, with no click.
Use `chip-group` when the person chooses among several filter options.
Use `button` with a label when the action is used often: here the name only appears after a click.

teclado.acao: On the main button, open or close the control; on the extra action, run `action.onClick`.
With the control open, closes it and returns focus to the main button.

acessibilidade: The main button has `aria-expanded` and an `aria-label` equal to `label`, open or closed; the visible label and `detail` are `aria-hidden`, so anything that is only in `detail` is not announced.
The extra action is a second `<button>` with `aria-label` and `title` from `action.label`; it only exists with the control open and comes right after the main one in the `Tab` order.
movimento: On open, the width grows on a spring with no overshoot and the label slides 8 px out of a slight blur; on close, it fades quickly while the width shrinks, and neighbors follow with no jump.
The icon stays still in a box the size of the closed control and shrinks to 0.86 on press; the extra action shrinks to 0.9.
With “reduce motion”, the label and the action only fade, the width changes at once, and the press does not change the scale.
notasIA: To keep only one open at a time, control it in the parent: `expanded={aberto === "share"}` and `onExpandedChange={v => setAberto(v ? "share" : null)}`.
`action` takes `icon`, `label`, and `onClick` and only appears with the control open; `detail` adds text after the label, like a count.
`tone="accent"` fills with the accent color when open, and `variant="chip"` is the compact version, 2rem tall, for filters and tags.

quandoUsar: Actions on a message or a list item where only one needs a visible name at a time: Reply, Archive, Flag, Delete.
Quick actions that confirm on the button itself with a past-tense word, like Archive becoming Archived, with no toast.
quandoEvitar: Use `floating-button-group` or `button-group` when all labels should be visible at the same time.
Use `confirm-morph` or `hold-to-confirm` for deletions that need confirmation: here `tone="danger"` only changes the color, and the action runs on click.
Avoid on touch-only screens for urgent actions: with no hover, the first tap only reveals the label and a second one is needed to run it.

teclado.acao: Enters and leaves the group in a single stop; focus returns to the last focused action.
Move focus between actions and wrap around at the ends; the focused action expands and shows the label.
Go to the first and last action.
Run the focused action; with `doneLabel`, it confirms in place.

acessibilidade: The group is `role="toolbar"` with the required `label` and a roving tabindex; each button has an `aria-label` equal to the item's `label`, even when collapsed.
`disabled` items use `aria-disabled`, stay focusable, and show the label, so the person can discover what they would do; while the `onSelect` Promise runs, the button gets `aria-busy`.
The confirmation (`doneLabel`) is announced by a `role="status"`, including when the same action repeats.
movimento: The action under the mouse or in focus opens its width on a spring with no overshoot and the label slides out from behind the icon; the neighbors collapse, and the whole group follows the width.

On confirm, the icon becomes a checkmark that draws itself and the word swaps to `doneLabel` without changing the width, which already reserves the larger of the two; with a pending Promise, the icon pulses.
With “reduce motion”, the width changes at once, the label only fades, the icon does not shrink on press, and the wait pulse becomes a fixed opacity.
notasIA: Each item needs `id`, a short `label` (a verb), and `icon`; `onSelect` can return a Promise, and returning `false` or rejecting skips the confirmation.
`doneLabel` (“Archived”) turns on the in-place confirmation for `confirmDuration` ms (1400); omit it on actions that open something, like Reply.
One action is always expanded: `defaultExpanded` chooses which (by default, the first enabled one), and `onAction(id)` runs before the item's `onSelect`.

quandoUsar: Action bars over a board or document, like Undo, Redo, Present, and Share, with shortcut hints in the tooltip.
Floating bars over a selection or over the content (`variant="floating"`), with icons only and the name in a tooltip.
quandoEvitar: Use `button-group` when the actions should form a single surface with dividers or need an attached menu.
Use `toggle-group` when the buttons are options that turn on and off together, like bold and italic.
Use `overflow-actions` when the bar needs to fit varying widths: this tray does not collapse or wrap.

teclado.acao: Enters and leaves the bar in a single stop; focus returns to the last focused action.
Move focus between enabled actions and wrap around at the ends; in the `vertical` orientation, use `↓` and `↑`.
Go to the first and last enabled action.
Run the focused action; the highlight darkens while the key is held down.
Closes the open tooltip (Radix behavior).

acessibilidade: The tray is `role="toolbar"` with `aria-orientation` and a roving tabindex; each button has an `aria-label` equal to `label`, and `pressed` becomes `aria-pressed` for mode actions, like Present.
Icon-only items or items with `shortcut` get a tooltip with the name and shortcut, on mouse hover or keyboard focus; `shortcut` is only a hint, the component does not register the key.
`disabled` items get `aria-disabled` and are skipped by the arrows, by `Home`, and by `End`.
movimento: A single highlight moves and resizes to the button under the pointer or in focus, on a spring with no overshoot; coming from nothing, it appears in place growing from 0.94, and fades when the pointer leaves.
On press, the highlight darkens and shrinks to 0.965 in place; a new label, like Share → Copied, rises from a slight blur without changing the width if it is in `reserveLabels`.
With “reduce motion”, the highlight jumps to the button with no scale and colors change almost instantly.
responsivo: The tray always keeps its natural size: it does not wrap or clip buttons, so on a narrow screen it overflows; use `iconOnly` or fewer items.
In the `vertical` orientation, tooltips open to the right by default (`tooltipSide`), so they do not cover the neighboring button.
notasIA: Depends on `tooltip`, installed alongside; each action needs `id` and `label`, and an item `{ type: "separator" }` draws a divider.
For mode actions, pass `pressed` controlled by the parent and toggle it in `onSelect`; `onAction(id)` runs after the item's `onSelect`, good for logging usage.
If a label changes after the click, list all the texts in `reserveLabels`; `iconOnly` on the group applies to all items, and each item's `iconOnly` takes priority.

quandoUsar: Destructive or hard-to-undo actions whose consequences are already visible on screen, like deleting the project that is open.
Actions where an accidental tap must not count and a dialog would be heavy: publish, archive, release a shipment.
quandoEvitar: Use `dialog` when the person needs to read the consequences before confirming.
Use `confirm-morph` when the confirmation should offer Cancel, show progress, and allow Undo in place.
Use `toast-action` with Undo for frequent, reversible actions: holding on every use slows the flow.

teclado.acao: Held down on the button, they advance the fill; releasing before the end undoes it, and completing calls `onConfirm`.

acessibilidade: It is a `<button>` with `aria-describedby` pointing to a hidden instruction (“Press and hold for 1.2 seconds to confirm…”, fixed in English); on completion, it gets `aria-disabled` and a `role="status"` announces `confirmedLabel`.
The `aria-label` follows the visible text (`label`, then `confirmedLabel`); a quick click or tap does not confirm, so say in the `label` that holding is required, like “Hold to delete project”.
Dragging the pointer more than 24 px outside the button, or taking focus away from it, cancels the press.
movimento: The fill advances at a linear pace for `duration` ms, like an inverted copy of the button revealed from the left (the text changes color at the edge); releasing early rewinds it on a spring, and pressing again continues from where it stopped.
On press, the button shrinks slightly (0.97); on completion, the icon becomes a checkmark that draws itself and the width follows the new label on a spring with no overshoot.
With “reduce motion”, the fill still advances while held (it is the timer), but returns at once on release; there is no scale, and label and icon only fade.
notasIA: `onConfirm` runs once, on completion; afterward the button stays done until it remounts (the demo changes the `key`) or, in controlled mode, until `confirmed` goes back to `false`.
`tone="danger"` is for irreversible actions (the default `accent` uses the accent color); `duration` sets the time (1200 ms) and `icon` replaces the default trash can.
Use `onHoldChange` for a hint around it, like “Keep holding…”; `confirmedLabel` defaults to English (“Done”), and the hidden instruction only changes in the installed file.

quandoUsar: Navigation rows, menus, and icon bars where a shared background should follow the pointer and rest on the current section (`value`).
When you want the effect on your own items: any element with `data-highlight-item`, at any depth, gets the pill.
quandoEvitar: Use `tabs` or `segmented-control` when the chosen item swaps the displayed content: here there is no `role="tablist"` or panels.
Use `dropdown-menu` or `context-menu` when the actions should live in a floating menu, with menu semantics.
Use `floating-button-group` for a ready-made action bar, with tooltips and a single `Tab` stop.

teclado.acao: In the `vertical` orientation (default), move focus between enabled items and wrap around at the ends; in `horizontal`, use `→` and `←`.
Go to the first and last enabled item; arrows, `Home`, and `End` are turned off with `arrowNavigation={false}`.
Trigger the focused item, and an item with `value` becomes the selected one; items with `href` are links and respond only to `Enter`.

acessibilidade: The group is a `<div>` with no role: pass `role` and `aria-label`, like `role="toolbar"` or `role="group"`, as the demo does.
Items are `<button>` or, with `href`, links; the selected one gets `aria-current="true"`, and `disabled` disables the button or removes the link's `href` and sets `aria-disabled`.
The pill is decorative (`aria-hidden`), and each item remains a `Tab` stop, in addition to the arrows.
movimento: A single pill background slides and resizes to the item under the pointer or with keyboard focus, on a spring with no overshoot, and returns to the selected one when the pointer leaves; between two items it stays on the last one, without flickering.
While an item is pressed, the pill shrinks to 0.97 and releases on a spring curve.
With “reduce motion”, the pill jumps straight to the item and does not shrink on press.
responsivo: In the `horizontal` orientation, items wrap by default (`flex-flow: row wrap`) and the pill follows to the new line; pass `style={{ flexWrap: "nowrap" }}` to keep a single row.
When the group size changes (a font loading, a section opening, a window resized), the pill repositions without animating.
notasIA: Build with `<HoverHighlight>` and `<HoverHighlightItem>` children; give items a `value` and control selection with `value` and `onValueChange` on the group, or use `defaultValue`.
Items without `value` only get the hover highlight; `tone="accent"` uses the accent color with dark text, and `--hover-highlight-radius` changes the pill radius.

`HoverHighlightItem` forwards props to the `<button>` or `<a>` (like `aria-label` and `style`); its `onClick` runs before the selection, and `event.preventDefault()` in it prevents the item from being selected.

quandoUsar: Toggle buttons whose icon represents the state: open and close the menu, play and pause, enable and mute notifications, like.
Small confirmations inside your own button, like copy becoming a checkmark or add becoming a checkmark (`copy` and `plus`).
quandoEvitar: Use `copy-button` when you need to copy a value with the confirmation ready-made.
Use `theme-switch` to toggle between light and dark: it is already a complete button, with the animated icon and the accessible name.
For an icon that does not change state, use the regular icon from the Lucide library; here there are only eight fixed pairs of drawings.
acessibilidade: Every icon is an SVG with `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`: put it in a `<button>` that has the accessible name and `aria-pressed` reflecting `state`.
Since the drawing changes with the state (the menu becomes an X, play becomes pause), update the button name along with it, for example from “Open menu” to “Close menu”.
movimento: The icon transforms instead of swapping: the menu lines rotate into an X, play splits into two bars, the sun grows while a shadow carves out the moon, all on springs that can be interrupted midway.
Turning the bell on makes it swing (0.9 s), with the clapper delayed, and liking the heart fires a ring and sparks once; turning it off strikes the bell through, and unliking only empties the heart.
With “reduce motion”, the icon changes state instantly, without the bell swing or the heart burst.
notasIA: Use `<IconMorph name="menu" state={aberto} />` or the specific component: `MenuIcon`, `PlayPauseIcon`, `PlusCheckIcon`, `CopyCheckIcon`, `SunMoonIcon`, `ChevronIcon`, `BellIcon`, or `HeartIcon`.
The parent controls `state`, since the icon has no click or state of its own; `size` (24) and `strokeWidth` (1.75) tune the drawing, and `ChevronIcon` accepts `turn` (degrees) and `pointing`.
It inherits the text color (`currentColor`); the liked heart uses `--icon-morph-like`, which by default is the danger color.

quandoUsar: Quick acknowledgment of a post, comment, or release note, with the count of each reaction and your own highlighted.
When the set of possible reactions is fixed and short (`options`) and only those that already have votes should appear in the bar.
quandoEvitar: Use `comment-thread` when the person needs to reply with text, not just react.
Use `icon-morph` with `name="heart"` inside your own button when there is a single like reaction, with no count per type.

teclado.acao: On a pill, add or remove your reaction; on the add button, open the picker with focus on the first option.
In the picker, move focus between options and wrap around at the ends; `↓` and `↑` do the same.
In the picker, go to the first and last option.
Closes the picker and returns focus to the add button; choosing an option with `Enter` or `Space` does the same and applies the reaction.

acessibilidade: The bar is `role="group"` with `label` as its name; each pill is a button with `aria-pressed` and a name with the reaction and the count, like “Love, 11 reactions, including yours”.

The add button opens a Radix dialog with a `role="toolbar"` bar of options on a roving tabindex; each change is announced in a `role="status"`, and if the focused pill disappears, focus moves to its neighbor.

Names and announcements are built in English in the code (“reactions”, “including yours”, “Add reaction”, “Added …”); in a Portuguese interface, translate those strings in the installed file and pass `label`.
movimento: The count digits roll in the direction of the change, up when it increases and down when it decreases, and only the ones that change move; on reacting, the icon gets a spring impulse in scale and rotation.
New pills appear at half scale out of a blur, the others slide to make room, and the bar height follows on a spring when wrapping; the picker grows from the button, with the options in sequence.
With “reduce motion”, numbers swap without rolling, the icon does not hop, pills only fade, and the picker appears without growing.
responsivo: Pills wrap according to the width, and the bar height changes on a spring instead of pushing the content below all at once; the picker opens above the button and stays 12 px from the window edges.
notasIA: In `options`, `icon` is the Lucide component (`ThumbsUp`), not an element (`<ThumbsUp />`); each reaction in `value` or `defaultValue` is `{ id, count, reacted }`.
When controlled, keep the list that arrives in `onValueChange(next, change)` and return it in `value`; pills follow the list order, and a reaction with `count` 0 leaves the bar.
The bar only counts: it does not know who reacted nor talk to the server; send `change` (`id` and `reacted`) to your API.

quandoUsar: A main action with a few close alternatives in the menu, like Send, with Schedule and Save draft alongside.
When the last chosen alternative should become the main action: change `label` and `icon` in `onSelect` and the button transforms in place.
Exports with a default format and others in the menu, in the `secondary` variant.
quandoEvitar: Use `dropdown-menu` when there is no clearly main action.
Use `button-group` when the actions are independent and all deserve to stay in view.
Use `action-swap` when the action changes state on its own with each click, without the person choosing from a menu.

teclado.acao: On the main button, run `onClick`; on the arrow, open the menu with focus on the first alternative (`↓` also opens).
In the menu, move through the enabled alternatives and wrap around at the ends.
In the menu, go to the first and last alternative.
In the menu, typing the start of a label moves focus to that alternative.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the arrow; choosing an alternative with `Enter` or `Space` also closes it.

acessibilidade: There are two buttons: the main one, whose name is `label` (the animated text is `aria-hidden` and a hidden copy in `aria-live="polite"` announces the swap), and the arrow, with an `aria-label` built in English (“Send more actions”).
The menu is Radix's `DropdownMenu` in modal mode: while open, focus is trapped in it and the page does not scroll; on close, focus returns to the arrow.
`disabled` turns off both halves together; `disabled` alternatives are dimmed and skipped by the arrows.
movimento: When `label` changes, the shared letters stay still and only the new ones rise from a slight blur, in sequence; the icon swaps with scale, and the width follows on a spring with no overshoot.
Pressing the main action shrinks the whole pill to 0.97; the arrow responds only with color, so Radix measures the anchor without scale, and rotates 180° with the menu open.
The menu grows from the arrow, with the alternatives in sequence; with “reduce motion”, letters and width swap instantly, the pill does not shrink, and the menu only fades.
notasIA: `label` and `onClick` are the main action; `actions` lists the alternatives (`label`, `onSelect`, `icon`, `disabled`, `destructive`), and each one's `label` is the React key, so do not repeat labels.
The component does not swap the main action on its own: to remember the last choice, keep it in the parent's state and pass the new `label` and `icon`, as the demo does.
The arrow's `aria-label` is built in English (“… more actions”): in a Portuguese interface, adjust that string in the installed file; `variant="secondary"` is the lighter, smaller version.

quandoUsar: Short lists for quick triage, especially on touch, like an inbox: archive, delete, mark as unread.
When each row needs two or three frequent actions without taking fixed space, with the more-actions menu as the path for keyboard and screen reader.
quandoEvitar: Use `context-menu` or `dropdown-menu` when the list is used mostly with mouse and keyboard: here the gesture is the main shortcut.
Use `reorderable-list` when dragging should change the order of items.
Avoid in long or virtualized lists: each row measures its own width, stacks one animated layer per action, and animates the height on enter and exit.

teclado.acao: Moves through each row's more-actions button; the actions revealed by the gesture are outside the tab order.
On the more-actions button, open the row menu, with the same actions as the gesture.
In the menu, move through the actions and wrap around at the ends; `Enter` or `Space` run the focused action.
Collapses the row that is open from the gesture; with the row menu open, closes the menu and returns focus to the button.

acessibilidade: The list is a `<ul role="list">` with `label` as its name; each row has a button with a name built in English (“More actions for …”, from the row's `label`) that opens a Radix menu with the same actions.

The actions revealed by the gesture are `aria-hidden` and outside `Tab`: the menu is the path for keyboard and screen reader, and when the row leaves through it, focus goes to the neighboring row's button.
Give the row a `label` that identifies the item, like the message subject, and give actions with `tone="danger"` a label that says the outcome, like “Delete”.
movimento: The row follows the finger or mouse after 8 px horizontally (vertical movement stays with scrolling) and resists like a rubber band past the last stop; on release, the velocity decides whether it opens, closes, or runs.
A long swipe, past about 56% of the width, arms the outermost action, which stretches over the whole row; the row exits in the direction of the gesture and the list closes the gap on a spring.
With “reduce motion”, the row jumps to each stop, removal is only a fade, and the menu appears without growing.
responsivo: Each action takes 76 px when the row rests open; on narrow screens, prefer one or two per side.
On touch, `touch-action: pan-y` leaves vertical scrolling to the page; with a mouse, the row shows the drag cursor.
desempenho: Each row keeps a `ResizeObserver` and one animated layer per action; the component was made for short triage lists, not for thousands of rows.
notasIA: Build `<SwipeActions label="Caixa de entrada">` with one `<SwipeActionsRow key={id} label={assunto} leading={…} trailing={…}>` per item; the stable `key` allows the animated exit and the return on an Undo.
In `onSelect`, remove the item from the state (the row leaves and the list closes the gap); for actions that keep the item, like mark as unread, use `keepRow`.
The outermost action on each side (`leading[0]` and the last of `trailing`) is the one that runs on the long swipe; `fullSwipe={false}` turns off that shortcut.

quandoUsar: A light/dark toggle button in the app or site bar, with the sun and moon rotating in place.
When the theme change is going to get a full-page transition: the button hands the variant and the element itself to `onThemeChange`, so the animation starts from it (`reveal`, the default).
quandoEvitar: Use the `user-menu` theme selector, or a `segmented-control`, when the person should also be able to choose “System”: here there are only light and dark.
Use `switch` when the theme is an option on a settings page, next to other toggles.
Use `icon-morph` with `name="theme"` when the button already exists and you only want the transforming sun and moon icon.

teclado.acao: Trigger the button, which calls `onThemeChange` with the next theme.

acessibilidade: It is the library's `button`, with `aria-pressed` true in the dark theme; the icons are `aria-hidden`.
Without `label`, the name is built in English and changes with the state (“Switch to light mode”), which is confusing next to `aria-pressed`; pass a fixed `label`, like “Dark theme”.
The visible text “Switch theme” is fixed in English and, with `aria-label`, stops being the button's name; in a Portuguese interface, use `iconOnly` or replace that text in the installed file.
movimento: On the swap, the sun and moon rotate in the same direction (clockwise toward dark), with scale on a short spring and a fade with a slight blur; in dark, the `reveal` variant also enlarges the icon to 1.08.
A saved preference that arrives right after hydration swaps the icon without animating, so a page that opens in dark does not rotate the button.
With “reduce motion”, the icon only fades, the variant adjustment happens without transition, and the button press does not scale.
notasIA: The component neither switches the theme nor animates the page: it calls `onThemeChange(next, variant, trigger)`, and the app applies the theme (for example, `data-theme` on `<html>`) and, if you want, the transition.

The demo's transition comes from the site, not from the installed item: `document.startViewTransition` and an animated `clip-path` on `::view-transition-new(root)`, starting from `trigger`, skipped with “reduce motion”.
`theme` is controlled and only accepts `light` or `dark` (resolve “system” before passing it); the other variants are `eclipse`, `split`, and `rise`.

quandoUsar: A theme button in an app bar, as in the demo, when the swap should cross the screen like a disc entering from the side.
When the theme rarely changes and a longer transition fits: in the demo, the eclipse takes 720 ms, versus 520 to 560 ms for the other variants.
quandoEvitar: Use `theme-switch` (`reveal` variant) when the transition should start from the button itself, where the person clicked.
Use `theme-switch-rise` or `theme-switch-split` for a shorter swap.

teclado.acao: Trigger the button, which calls `onThemeChange` with the next theme and `"eclipse"`.

acessibilidade: It is the library's `button`, with `aria-pressed` true in the dark theme and `aria-hidden` icons; icon-only (`iconOnly`, as in the demo), `label` is the only name, so pass fixed text, like “Change appearance”.
Without `label`, the default name is built in English and changes with the state (“Switch to light mode”); outside `iconOnly`, the visible text is the fixed “Switch theme”.
movimento: With `variant="eclipse"`, the icon shifts 2 px to the left in the dark theme, on a spring curve, and returns when going back to light; the sun and moon swap by rotating.
The page crossing does not come with the component: in the demo, a circle the size of the screen diagonal starts from outside, on the left, until it covers the screen, via View Transitions.
With “reduce motion”, the icon only fades and the shift happens without transition; the demo's utility also swaps the theme without animating the page.
notasIA: It is the same `ThemeSwitch` with `variant="eclipse"`: import from `@/components/ryan-ui/theme-switch/theme-switch`; `onThemeChange` receives `"eclipse"` as the second argument.

Implement the crossing in the app: inside `document.startViewTransition`, apply the theme and animate the `clip-path` of `::view-transition-new(root)` from `circle(D at -D 50%)` to `circle(D at 50% 50%)`, with D the screen diagonal.
`theme` is controlled and only accepts `light` or `dark`; skip the animation when `prefers-reduced-motion` is on, as the demo does.

quandoUsar: A theme button near the bottom of the screen or in a lower corner, as in the demo, when the new theme should rise from the bottom edge.
When the transition should be a straight, simple movement that does not depend on where the button is.
quandoEvitar: Use `theme-switch` (`reveal` variant) when the transition should start at the click point.
Use `theme-switch-split` when the button sits at the center of a bar and a symmetric opening fits better.

teclado.acao: Trigger the button, which calls `onThemeChange` with the next theme and `"rise"`.

acessibilidade: It is the library's `button`, with `aria-pressed` true in the dark theme and `aria-hidden` icons; icon-only (`iconOnly`, as in the demo), `label` is the only name, so pass fixed text, like “Change appearance”.
Without `label`, the default name is built in English and changes with the state (“Switch to light mode”); outside `iconOnly`, the visible text is the fixed “Switch theme”.
movimento: With `variant="rise"`, the icon rises 2 px in the dark theme, on a spring curve, and drops when going back to light, while the sun and moon swap by rotating.

The page rise does not come with the component: in the demo, the new theme is revealed from bottom to top in 520 ms, clipping `::view-transition-new(root)` from `inset(100% 0 0 0)` to `inset(0 0 0 0)`.
With “reduce motion”, the icon only fades and the shift happens without transition; the demo's utility also swaps the theme without animating the page.
notasIA: It is the same `ThemeSwitch` with `variant="rise"`: import from `@/components/ryan-ui/theme-switch/theme-switch`; `onThemeChange` receives `"rise"` as the second argument.

Implement the rise in the app: inside `document.startViewTransition`, apply the theme and animate the `clip-path` of `::view-transition-new(root)`; since it does not start from the button, `trigger` can be ignored.
In the demo, the button floats in the bottom right corner of a frame (`position: absolute` on the parent); the component does not position itself.

quandoUsar: A centered theme button or one in a symmetric bar, when the new theme should open from a vertical slit in the middle of the screen.
When you want a short, symmetric swap (520 ms in the demo) that does not depend on where the button is.
quandoEvitar: Use `theme-switch` (`reveal` variant) when the transition should start from the button itself.
Use `theme-switch-rise` when the button is near the bottom of the screen and a rise fits better.

teclado.acao: Trigger the button, which calls `onThemeChange` with the next theme and `"split"`.

acessibilidade: It is the library's `button`, with `aria-pressed` true in the dark theme and `aria-hidden` icons; the demo shows the version with text and the icon-only one, both with the fixed `label` “Change appearance”.

In the version with text, the visible label is the fixed “Switch theme”, in English, and is not the button's name when there is a `label`; in a Portuguese interface, use `iconOnly` or replace that text in the installed file.
movimento: With `variant="split"`, the icon shifts 1 px to the right in the dark theme, on a spring curve, and returns when going back to light, while the sun and moon swap by rotating.

The page opening does not come with the component: in the demo, the new theme appears from a slit in the center that opens to the sides, clipping `::view-transition-new(root)` from `inset(0 50% 0 50%)` to `inset(0 0 0 0)`.
With “reduce motion”, the icon only fades and the shift happens without transition; the demo's utility also swaps the theme without animating the page.
notasIA: It is the same `ThemeSwitch` with `variant="split"`: import from `@/components/ryan-ui/theme-switch/theme-switch`; `onThemeChange` receives `"split"` as the second argument.
Implement the opening in the app: inside `document.startViewTransition`, apply the theme and animate the `clip-path` of `::view-transition-new(root)`; `trigger` is not needed for this variant.
`theme` is controlled and only accepts `light` or `dark`; skip the animation when `prefers-reduced-motion` is on, as the demo does.

quandoUsar: The account menu behind the person's photo in the app's top bar: identity, account shortcuts, theme, and sign out.
Apps with presence (Available, Busy, Away), where the person changes status without leaving the screen.
Interfaces that need the same menu on mobile: below 640 px it becomes a bottom sheet with no extra configuration.
quandoEvitar: Use `dropdown-menu` for general action menus, without the person's identity or selectors.
Avoid for long lists of destinations: the code itself recommends three or four items; larger navigation belongs in `site-header` or a sidebar like `animated-sidebar`.

teclado.acao: On the avatar, open the menu with focus on the first row; `↑` opens with focus on the last.
In the menu, move through rows and selectors and wrap around at the ends; `Home` and `End` go to the ends.
On a selector (Status or Theme), instantly choose the previous or next option, without closing the menu.
Typing the start of a label moves focus to the matching row.
Trigger the focused row; items and Sign out close the menu, and status and theme choices keep it open.
Close the menu and return focus to the avatar.

acessibilidade: The avatar is a button with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, and a name built in English (“Account menu, Emma Collins, Available”); the panel is `role="menu"` labeled by it, and Status and Theme use `menuitemradio`.

Focus only enters the menu when someone opens it (a menu that starts open does not steal focus) and returns to the avatar on close; on mobile, the sheet has `aria-modal`, a scrim, and locks page scrolling.
Status combines color and shape (filled circle, bar, or ring), without relying on color alone; the texts for Status, Theme, Sign out, and the options are fixed in English in the code.
movimento: On desktop, the panel grows from the center of the avatar on a spring with no overshoot, with rows entering in sequence, and closes with a short fade; a single highlight slides between rows.
On mobile, the sheet rises from the base and can be dragged down to close (more than 80 px or a quick gesture); changing the status transforms the dot, opening the away hole or the busy bar.
With “reduce motion”, panel and sheet only fade, the sheet does not drag, color and shape transitions are turned off, and the sign-out indicator spins more slowly.
responsivo: Below 640 px of width, the same content opens as a bottom sheet with a scrim, taller rows, and without the shortcut hints; the name next to the avatar (`showName`) also disappears.
On desktop, the panel is 15.5rem wide, stays 12 px from the edges, opens below the avatar and flips upward when there is not enough room, repositioning on scroll or resize.
notasIA: Pass `user` (`name`, `email`, and, if you want, `plan` and `avatarSrc`, with initials when the photo is missing); the status only appears with `status` or `onStatusChange`, because `defaultStatus` alone does not show it.
`onThemeChange` only reports the choice (`light`, `dark`, or `system`); applying the theme to the page is up to the app, and `showTheme={false}` hides the selector.
`onSignOut` can return a Promise: the item shows progress and the menu closes when it finishes; each item's `keys` (like `["⌘", ","]`) are only a visual hint.
